title: Funan
capsule: Funan was the first major Indianized polity in mainland Southeast Asia, occupying the lower Mekong delta and coastal Cambodia from approximately the 1st century CE and controlling maritime trade routes between India and China. Chinese envoys in the 3rd century described a wealthy kingdom with walled cities, written laws, tax collection in gold and silver, and a palace culture that veneered Hindu brahmanical ritual over local traditions. The kingdom reached its zenith under Fan Shiman and his successors in the 3rd century, extending tributary networks across much of coastal Indochina, but by the 6th century the inland successor state of Chenla had effectively absorbed Funan's core territories, and Chinese sources cease to mention Funan as a distinct entity after the mid-7th century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Funan's territorial extent is highly conjectural; no indigenous inscriptions unambiguously define its boundaries, and the map geometry is derived from Chinese tribute-mission accounts and French colonial archaeological surveys of the Oc Eo site complex, which may represent only the commercial heartland.
